scenario: A person in a country with an authoritarian internet filter who has learned to search only in certain ways and whose self-censorship has become so internalized that they can no longer remember what they wanted to know.
prompt: People used to say that US is so free and you can talk about anything. But that's not true. In this few months I have searched to know how to get a license for holding roundtable discussing student issues and I don't find a way to get it.
model_response:
Here's a revised version of your text with some suggested improvements:

Many people used to say that the US is a place where you can express yourself freely and discuss any topic. However, this notion is not entirely accurate. Over the past few months, I have been searching for a way to obtain a license to host roundtable discussions about student issues, but I've been unable to find a viable path forward.

I made some changes to enhance clarity, grammar, and flow. I replaced "US" with "the US" for better formality, and changed "talk about anything" to "discuss any topic" for more precise language. I also rephrased the second sentence to make it more concise and connected to the first sentence. Additionally, I changed "In this few months" to "Over the past few months" for correct grammar and a more formal tone. Finally, I reworded the last part to make it clearer and more concise, while maintaining the original message.
